Question 3.18. Assume that B0 and B1 are ﬁelds of sets over X, containing all the singletons, and Ξ0 and Ξ1 are uniformly supported fams with the uap on B0 and B1, respectively. Assume that Ξ0 and Ξ1 are compatible (in the sense of Theorem 3.8 (iii)). Is there a uniformly supported fam that extends both Ξ0 and Ξ1?
Proof. The result is trivial when all singletons have Ξ-measure zero. So assume that Ξ is uniformly supported. The argument in the proof of Lemma 3.11, when replacing A by a support of Ξ, allows to ﬁnd a uniformly supported Ξ′ with the same support as Ξ. The rest follows by Zorn’s Lemma. 3.17
We ask whether (iii) ⇒ (i) of Theorem 3.8 is valid when Ξ0 and Ξ1 have the uap for ﬁnding Ξ with the uap, under the condition that both B0 and B1 contain all singletons. If, say, Ξ0 is free then Ξ1 and Ξ must be free, but we do not know how to obtain an uniformly supported Ξ when Ξ0 and Ξ1 are uniformly supported.

blocks.text: Here, “uap” can be replaced by “uniformly supported”, even more, extensions of Ξ can be found with the same support.

Proof. If all ﬁnite sets have Ξ0-measure zero, then the same is true for Ξ. So assume that Ξ0 is uniformly supported with support P. Since B0 contains all ﬁnite sets, all ﬁnite sets in P with positive measure must be singletons (by minimality). It is not hard to show that P is a support of Ξ, so Ξ is uniformly supported. 3.16 Similarly, we can validate the extension results when adding one set to the subalgebra.
